title: Neurosyphilis presenting with Guillain–Barre syndrome: a case report
case_prompt:
A previously healthy 37-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a three-month history of constant severe headache and photophobia, a two-month history of a pruritic rash on her chest, neck, palms, and soles, and two weeks of progressive arm weakness and numbness. When her weakness progressed to difficulty swallowing, she sought emergency care. She denied fever but reported intermittent chills over the prior three months.

On examination, she had bilateral cranial nerve V, VI, and VII palsies and bilateral optic nerve head edema. Near visual acuity was 20/20, color vision intact, and pupils were equal and reactive without relative afferent pupillary defect. Motor testing revealed neck flexion strength 4/5, distal greater than proximal bilateral upper extremity weakness (3/5), and absent reflexes throughout. Sensation was markedly decreased to all modalities in a stocking–glove distribution and circumferentially below the neck to the waist. The skin exam showed thin scaly papules on the upper chest and neck, more erythematous papules on the back and flanks, and faint erythematous macules on the palms and soles.

Given the combination of weakness, numbness, and areflexia suggestive of polyradiculopathy, along with atypical headache, papilledema, and rash, a broad diagnostic workup was undertaken. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head with contrast demonstrated bilateral cranial nerve V, VII, and VIII enhancement. Spine imaging showed only mild C5–6 stenosis. Lumbar puncture revealed an opening pressure of 36 cm H2O, 6 WBC/mm3, protein 46 mg/dL, and glucose 63 mg/dL. A CSF infectious PCR panel for 14 pathogens and HIV PCR were negative. Serologies for Coxsackievirus and Campylobacter jejuni, and anti-ganglioside antibodies for Miller-Fisher syndrome were negative. Rheumatologic screening, including ACE level, ANA, ANCA, and SSA/B, was unremarkable.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. GBS considered because of ascending weakness, sensory loss, and areflexia — “the patient’s presentation thus far of weakness, numbness, and areflexia were suggestive of a polyradiculopathy, such as that as seen in GBS.”
2. Bacterial, viral, and fungal meningitis considered but excluded by negative CSF PCR panel — “CSF Infectious PCR panel for 14 bacteria, viruses, and yeast … as well as an HIV PCR, was negative.”
3. Miller-Fisher syndrome variant considered but excluded by negative anti-ganglioside antibodies — “Anti-ganglioside antibodies for Miller-Fisher syndrome were negative.”
4. Rheumatologic and systemic inflammatory etiologies such as sarcoidosis and ANCA vasculitis considered but excluded by unremarkable screening labs — “screening labs including Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme levels, ANA, ANCA, and SSA/B were unremarkable.”
5. Neurosyphilis confirmed by positive serum RPR and CSF VDRL — “serum RPR was positive in 1:128 titer, and CSF VDRL was positive with 1:1 titer, confirming neurosyphilis.”
6. Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy subtype established by electrodiagnostic testing — “These findings confirmed a mixed demyelinating polyneuropathy predominantly affecting motor nerves consistent with an acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy variant of GBS.”
